pins.title: Lost the trail? Stop first.
pins.sub: Then think, look around and plan.
pins.pinTitle: What to do if you get lost hiking: the STOP method, when to stay put and how to signal for help
pins.description: Lost the trail? Stop walking, stay calm and use STOP: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan. Call 911 if you have signal, stay put unless you can confidently retrace your route, and blow three short whistle blasts to call for help. Our step-by-step guide covers staying warm while you wait.

pins.title: Are trekking poles worth it?
pins.sub: Yes on steep descents. Less so on flat trails.
pins.pinTitle: Are trekking poles worth it? When they help your knees and when to skip them
pins.description: Trekking poles add balance on steep descents, loose rock, mud and stream crossings, and take some load off your knees going downhill. On short, flat trails they matter much less. Our guide covers one pole or two, how to size them and when to stow them.

pins.title: Glacier next summer? Plan it now.
pins.sub: The road, the shuttle and 12 day hikes.
pins.board: Best Day Hikes in US National Parks
pins.pinTitle: Glacier National Park trip planner: Going-to-the-Sun Road, Logan Pass shuttle and 12 day hikes
pins.description: Planning Glacier National Park for next summer? This 30-page printable guide covers when Going-to-the-Sun Road opens, Logan Pass shuttle and parking, sample 2, 3 and 5-day plans and 12 day hikes from easy to the Highline. Instant PDF download, US Letter and A4. Check nps.gov for your dates.

pins.title: Frosty trail? Pull on some grip.
pins.sub: Chain cleats that stretch over your boots.
pins.pinTitle: Chain ice cleats for hiking boots: grip on icy trails and packed snow
pins.description: Icy trailheads and packed-snow trails are where winter slips happen. These chain ice cleats stretch over hiking boots and winter shoes (about US women's 4 to US men's 11), with stainless steel chains and spikes and a storage bag. Not crampons: for icy paths and everyday winter hikes. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.
